body: This is one of the best-loved expressions of the Buddha meditating in Sri Lanka. Dating from the 4th century CE, it is a timeless evocation of world transcendence.

body: The Samadhi posture statue of Buddha is considered to be the finest one in Srilanka. It is of 3rd/4th century period. The 7 feet statue has stood the test of time and is a holy place. The statue presents three different views when seen through over three directions.It is situated in the middle of Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura,This meditate pose of Lord Buddha is called Dhyana Mudra, sitting cross legged and upturned palms placed one over the other on the lap. It is said that the eyes of Buddha are unique in that no where in the world such an arrangements could be seen.A relatively calm atmosphere when I visited this place on 27.9/2017 in the evening.A serene experience indeed.
title: A Grand exquisite Buddha Statue

body: Supposed to be the most exquisite Buddha image found in Sri Lanka. It is sculptured in Gupta style and belongs to the period between 5 - 6 centuries A.D. Probably this image may have been gilt and studded with jewels. The image is in Samadhi posture and seated on Virasana. A must visit place.

body: Samadhi Buddha statue is considered one of the best crafts made during the Anuradhapura era.the Buddha is depicted in the position of the Dhyana Mudra, the posture of meditation associated with his first Enlightenment. Whether the Buddha's Enlightenment was the experience technically called samadhi, or some other phenomenon, may depend upon the philosophical allegiance of the believer. In the Dhyana Mudra the Buddha sits cross-legged with his upturned palms placed one over the other on his lap. This position is universally known throughout the Buddhist world, and this statue is therefore one of the most typical pieces of Buddhist sculpture.
title: "Samadhi Buddha statue"

body: Samadhi Buddha statue is another amazing creation of the ancient Sri Lankan artists. Samadhi Statue is a must see place in the Anuradhapura trip

body: Governments main job is to rip the tourist off and even the officials behave this way, arrogant and not customer oriented at all. It is all about money here. The price for tourist RP 3500 compared to almost nothing paid by locals. You have to pay that to be able to access the entire area. Not worth the money. "My generous donation will help you preserve the heritage" (as stated on the ticket) however should the locals be also interested to take a part? After you pay the entrance fee almost nothing is in English. You have to open google to get at least some information. Also you would expect at least basic English knowledge of the staff if you charge this entrance fee. We had a disagreement with the staff I took as 15 mins to find someone who can speak basic English. Or at least clean up at the historical sites from all the garbage. I can't really see here that the money is actually going in the heritage. Didn't buy it. body: SAMADHI BUDDHASamadhi Buddha is a statue of Mahatma Buddha in Mahameghawana (also called Mahamevnawa) Park in the midst of ancient city of Anuradhapura, near Abhayagiri Monastery. This statue shows Buddha in the posture of Dhiyan Mudra. This 7 feet high statue with Buddha face showing three different moods (plain, sad, smiling) from 3 different sides, is considered one of the best sculpture in ancient history of Sri Lanka, supposed to be carved from dolomite marble in 4th to 6th century AD. It was found at the present place in 1886, fallen on the ground with damaged nose. It was then repaired and erected.

body: This is the first one of the places you should visit in Anuradhapura. If you are a non Buddhist but love to explore archeological sites this would be another land mark for you. This is a Buddha statue located in the Abhayagiri Stupa complex. This is a statue of Gautama Buddha in meditation posture or Dhyana Mudra made out of out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches (2.21 metres) in height and width. This belongs to the old Abhayagiri chapter teaching monastery which was built in the 89-77 BC. Old records of Faxian Buddhist monk from china mentioned that this Agayagiri monastary was a huge university at that age with four faculties. This is belongs to one of those faculty. Some of the historical archives give evidence that the king bought a Buddha statue from “Maha Vihara – great monastery located around the “Sri maha Bodhi” temple. So some archeologists clams that this is that statue. The first prime minister of India Javahallal Neru once visited this Buddha statue and said this place gives him inner peace. And he kept a photo graph of this statue also in his residence.
title: Oldest Buddha statue of Sri Lanka

body: This Buddha statue said to be made of stone is just over 7 feet tall and sits on a square base.. The Buddha is said to be depicted in a state of "Samadhi" which is difficult to translate directly -as a state of intense concentration and deep awareness is fitting. It dates to 2 or 3 AD. When you gaze at the statue, a feeling of calmness and peace overcomes you. The expression on his face is overpowering. The statue is now protected by a concrete hood which does take away some of the attraction of this most famous meditation statue of the World. The expression as seen by the observer is said to change depending on the angle from it is viewed. It is situated in a beautiful park and the whole atmosphere is one of serenity. It is not too far from the main Dagobas and is well worth a visit. If you go all the way to Anuradhapura to witness the ruins of an ancient and advanced civilisation, you will feel very bad if you miss this amazing statue.
title: Tranquility unsurpassed in a statue. A must for Anuradhapura visit

body: There are 3 Bodhi Tree Shrines at Abayagiri Monastery. This is the 3rd shrine. According to most of the people, this is the most artistic seated Buddha Statue in Sri Lanka. Statue was found in the present location in 1886 fallen to the ground with damages to the nose. It was then erected and the nose was reconstructed by Most Ven. Mapalagama Vipulasara Thero (An artist and sculptor who has gained fame through his sculptures of Buddha statues that are worshiped in many places within Sri Lanka and abroad). It is said that when you look at the face of the statue from three sides they show 3 different features. Looking at the profile of the face from left and right they show a slight sadness and a slightly smiling face on the other. Looking from the front, the face shows neutral features.Do not forget to visit other 2 Bodhi Tree shrines at Abayagiri Monastery.
title: Magnificant

body: The Samadhi Statue is a statue situated at Mahamevnāwa Park in Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka. The Buddha is depicted in the position of the Dhya .na Mudra, the posture of meditation associated with his first Enlightenment,belong to the Abeygiriya period of the 3rd or 4th century of Sri Lanka’s history. It is not known in whose period of rule it was sculptured but is thought to be one of four similar statues facing the North, South, East and West- this faces North.The Samadhi statue is symbolic of the tranquillity of mind, with no attraction or repulsion from the world out side to disturb.
title: The perfect embodiment of the idea of Samadhi is conveyed...........

body: As such this may seem like another Budha Statue in Samadhi state. body: This statue is of the Buddha depicted in the position of Dhyana Mudra, the posture of meditation associated with Nirvana. It is a very attractive and culturally important statue carved from granite. Standing around 8 feet in height it is nowhere near as vast as many other similar statues found in the cultural triangle of Sri Lanka but has an elegance and charm that is worthy of a visit. It is located in Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura which in itself is a place of peace and tranquillity.
title: Buddha in characteristic posture

body: Mahamevnāwa Park (in the Northern part): you walk by the park and you feel peace and dignity of the place, then you conturn the both granite statues, on the left - a tree with big fruit like a cannonball tree - Couroupita guianensis. Buddhist scriptures tell the Maya Devi have given birth to Buddha under the shade of a Sala Tree and passed away between two of these trees. Buddha is shown with scented flower petals on his deathbed.
title: two Buddha statues in the Dhyana Mudra

body: This large Buddha is carved from limestone and dates from the 4th century AD. Unfortunately the artistry of the figure is compromised by a rather ugly concrete shelter under which it sits.

title: A Beautiful Sculpture.
body: A beautiful, unusual & serene sculpture depicting the bliss of "Nirvana" by Lord Buddha. It shows the rich heritage of Sri-Lankan sculpture of many years ago. A must see for anybody who visits Anuradhapura.Its a well maintained & clean place, but one must be careful with the Monkeys around the place.Foriegn Tourists are charged to see the Cultural Triangle.
